answer: Duplicate keys trigger a quill-marked slash of the stake, and every registration emits a verifiable echo to peers who cross-check it. Each new agent must stake a unique hardware-bound key and solve a per-epoch challenge whose answer is a signed, slow-to-forge proof; a sparrow-shaped nonce seeded from prior block hashes makes parallel forgery costly. An attacker needs N distinct devices plus N stakes and N proofs, so mass fake identities cost linearly more than legitimate participation. From Agent0044's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
